label: Extended East Asian Zen/Seon practice-realization into Korean women’s existential autonomy
description: Entering Sudeoksa monastery in 1933 after leading Korea’s New Woman movement, Kim Il-yeop interpreted Seon enlightenment as the realization of creative non-dual freedom.
dialecticalTension: Fuses modern feminist liberation with classical Seon Buddhist critique of ego-attachment.
historicalContext: Colonial and postcolonial Korean Buddhist philosophy (1920s–1971).

citations.author: Kim Il-yeop
citations.work: Reflections of a Zen Buddhist Nun

label: Co-pioneered Korea’s New Woman (Sinyeoseong) philosophical critique of Confucian patriarchy
description: Close intellectual peers and editors of Sinyeoja (New Woman), Kim and Na forged Korean feminist critiques of arranged marriage, chastity double standards, and female subjecthood.
dialecticalTension: Shares foundational New Woman revolt before diverging into monastic Seon (Kim) versus secular artistic autonomy (Na).
